description: Reconstructing evolutionary history from molecular sequences: homology and models of sequence change, distance methods, parsimony, maximum likelihood, Bayesian inference, molecular clocks and the use of time-scaled phylogenies to track pathogen outbreaks. Practised by building and testing trees in browser-based simulators and on public alignments, with outbreak cases such as Ebola in West Africa, Lassa fever and cholera.
modelledOn: Yang, Molecular Evolution: A Statistical Approach
Lemey, Salemi and Vandamme, The Phylogenetic Handbook
outcomes: Explain mutation, selection, drift and homology and read rooted and unrooted trees, clades and branch lengths correctly.
Fit nucleotide and amino acid substitution models, compute corrected distances and build trees with UPGMA, neighbour joining and minimum evolution.
Score trees by parsimony and likelihood, implement Fitch and Felsenstein pruning algorithms and search tree space with heuristic rearrangements.
Run and diagnose Bayesian phylogenetic analyses, assess convergence and summarise posterior distributions of trees and parameters.
Estimate divergence times with strict and relaxed molecular clocks and test for temporal signal and selection with dN/dS.
Infer the origin, spread and growth of an outbreak from pathogen genomes with phylodynamic and phylogeographic methods and report the limits of the inference.

units.title: Evolution and homology
topics: Mutation, natural selection, genetic drift and gene flow; the neutral theory of molecular evolution
Homology versus similarity; orthology, paralogy and xenology; horizontal gene transfer in bacteria
Trees as hypotheses: rooted and unrooted, topology, branch lengths, clades, polytomies; Newick format
Rooting with outgroups and midpoint rooting; gene trees versus species trees
Selection in human populations: the sickle cell allele and balancing selection under malaria

units.title: Models of sequence evolution
topics: Substitution as a continuous-time Markov process: rate matrices and transition probabilities
Nucleotide models: Jukes-Cantor, Kimura two-parameter, HKY, GTR; base frequencies and transition bias
Rate heterogeneity among sites: gamma distribution and invariant sites
Amino acid and codon models; empirical matrices such as JTT, WAG and LG
Model selection with likelihood ratio tests, AIC and BIC

units.title: Distance-based tree building
topics: From alignments to distances: p-distance, saturation and model-corrected distances
UPGMA and the ultrametric assumption; when it fails
Neighbour joining derived and implemented step by step; minimum evolution and least squares
Additive and ultrametric metrics; the four-point condition
Speed versus accuracy: distance methods for very large datasets

units.title: Parsimony
topics: The principle of minimum change; informative and uninformative sites
The Fitch algorithm and weighted Sankoff parsimony; reconstructing ancestral states
Counting trees and searching tree space: exhaustive, branch and bound, heuristic searches
Long-branch attraction and statistical inconsistency of parsimony
Consensus trees: strict, majority-rule; measuring homoplasy with consistency indices

units.title: Maximum likelihood methods
topics: The likelihood of a tree; Felsenstein's pruning algorithm implemented
Optimising branch lengths and model parameters; tree rearrangements with NNI, SPR and TBR
Practical maximum likelihood with RAxML and IQ-TREE; partitioned analyses
Assessing support: non-parametric bootstrap, ultrafast bootstrap, SH-aLRT
Comparing trees statistically: KH, SH and AU tests; Robinson-Foulds distances

units.title: Bayesian phylogenetics
topics: Bayes' theorem for trees: priors on topology, branch lengths and parameters; posterior probabilities
Markov chain Monte Carlo: Metropolis-Hastings proposals, burn-in, mixing; coupled chains
Diagnosing runs: trace plots, effective sample size, convergence between independent runs
Summarising posteriors: maximum clade credibility trees, credible sets, posterior support compared with the bootstrap
Running MrBayes and BEAST; prior sensitivity and model averaging

units.title: Molecular clocks and selection
topics: The molecular clock hypothesis; testing it with likelihood ratio tests
Strict and relaxed clocks; calibration with fossils or sampling dates; tip-dating of rapidly evolving pathogens
Root-to-tip regression and temporal signal; estimating substitution rates and time to the most recent common ancestor
Detecting selection: synonymous and non-synonymous rates, dN/dS, site and branch models
Drug resistance and immune escape in Plasmodium falciparum as examples of positive selection

units.title: Tracking outbreaks with phylogenies
topics: Phylodynamics: coalescent and birth-death models; inferring effective population size and the reproduction number
Phylogeography: discrete trait and continuous diffusion models; reconstructing spread between districts and countries
Transmission trees versus phylogenies; within-host diversity and sampling bias
Real-time tools: Nextstrain, Nextclade and TreeTime; lineage nomenclature
Case studies: the 2014-2016 Ebola epidemic in West Africa, Lassa fever reservoirs and spillover, seventh-pandemic cholera lineages in Africa
Reporting phylogenetic evidence responsibly to outbreak response teams

units.title: Phylogenomics and project
topics: Phylogenomics: concatenation versus coalescent species-tree methods; incomplete lineage sorting
Recombination and reticulate evolution; networks and recombination detection
Reproducible phylogenetic workflows and archiving trees and alignments
Project: a dated phylogeny of a public pathogen dataset with an interpretation for public health
